summary: Defines MIB objects for configuring, monitoring, and controlling Data Link Switches. DLSw carries legacy link-layer traffic over IP networks, and this lets SNMP tools manage it.

eli5.summary: It is a control panel for devices that carry old-style network traffic across the modern internet.

questions: how to manage data link switching with snmp
how to configure a dlsw tcp partner with snmp
what is a dlsw transport connection
how to disconnect a dlsw circuit with snmp
subtitle: The SNMP objects for configuring, watching and controlling Data Link Switches that carry link-layer traffic over IP.

tldr.problem: Data Link Switches (DLSw) connect end stations across a network, but there was no standard SNMP way to configure, monitor and control them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the DLSW-MIB, with groups for the node, transport connections, interfaces, the directory of MAC addresses and NetBIOS names, circuits and SDLC end stations. It relies on the interface, SDLC and LLC MIBs instead of repeating them.
tldr.outcome: A manager can create transport connections, preload directory entries, investigate failed circuits and tune traps. The RFC discusses no security issues.

today: RFC 2024 is a Proposed Standard published in October 1996. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It describes management of DLSw as specified in RFC 1795.

sections.title: Purpose and the SNMP Framework
sections.content:
RFC 2024 extends the Management Information Base (MIB) for SNMP-based management. Its abstract says it defines objects for configuring, monitoring, and controlling Data Link Switches (DLSw), as described in RFC 1795. The module is written to comply with the SNMPv2 SMI and to be semantically identical to the SNMPv1 definitions.

It sits within the same three-part framework as other MIBs: the SMI (RFC 1902), MIB-II (RFC 1213), and the protocol (RFC 1157 and RFC 1905). The module is placed at mib-2 46.
sections.eli5: It is a rulebook for the dials and buttons on a special kind of network machine, so one manager program can talk to machines from many makers.

sections.title: Key Terms and Assumptions
sections.content:
The MIB defines its vocabulary up front. A transport connection is a full-duplex reliable connection between DLSw nodes. With TCP, RFC 1795 defines two TCP connections between a pair of nodes, each carrying data in one direction, and the transport connection is open only when both are operational. A circuit is the end-to-end association of two data link control entities through one or two DLSw nodes. A link station is one end of an LLC-2 connection, and DLSw ends LLC-2 at each DLSw node so keepalives and error recovery stay on each side of the LAN.

Key assumptions: the MIB manages a single DLSw entity, assumes the interface MIB, the SDLC MIB and the LLC-2 MIB (or equivalents) are implemented, and all MACs, SAPs and ring numbers are in non-canonical form, with the most significant bit transmitted first.
sections.eli5: A circuit is like a phone call between two people, and the transport connection is the long-distance line carrying many such calls between two switchboards.

sections.title: Relation to Other MIBs
sections.content:
The DLSw MIB does not copy information that lower-layer MIBs already hold. Each circuit entry instead points to a conceptual row in a data link control (DLC) MIB, such as the LLC or SDLC tables.

It also reuses ifIndex from the interfaces group (RFC 1573) to index dlswIfTable, to say where a MAC address or NetBIOS name can be reached, and to locate the local end station of a circuit. For SDLC (RFC 1747), dlswSdlcLsTable maps native SDLC addressing to the MAC and SAP used in the DLSw domain.

Because DLSw is the user of LLC services, the RFC says it is generally preferable to start administrative actions in the DLSw MIB. A hung circuit should be disconnected by setting dlswCircuitState, not by disabling the LLC part.
sections.eli5: The new control panel does not copy the gauges other panels already have. It just points to them, and you press the buttons on this panel first.

sections.title: Structure and Compliance
sections.content:
Objects fall into six groups under dlswMIB: dlswNode (node configuration, monitoring and control), dlswTConn (transport connections to partner nodes), dlswInterface (local interfaces), dlswDirectory (where MAC addresses and NetBIOS names are located), dlswCircuit (end-station connections) and dlswSdlc (SDLC-attached end stations).

Five compliance statements set minimum support. dlswCoreCompliance applies to all implementations. The others cover TCP transport, directory support, directory support with ordered retrieval, and SDLC end stations. NetBIOS objects are grouped separately because DLSw Version 1 does not require NetBIOS support.
sections.eli5: The panel has six sections, one for each part of the machine. Each maker only has to build the sections that match what their machine really does.

sections.title: How the MIB Is Meant to Be Used
sections.content:
To keep the MIB small, information shared between two partner nodes is defined only as what was received, with no objects for what was sent. To see the whole picture of a resource, a manager must query several DLSw nodes. The RFC also notes that the DLSw protocol gives no technique to match a partner's transport address to the address the management protocol uses.

Some changes are announced to partners in a run-time capabilities exchange, which a node unicasts to all active partners. Frequent changes could cause excess traffic, so managers should group such changes into a few SNMP SET requests, and agents should batch them, for example by sending the message only after no changes arrive for a pre-defined period.

Only a few objects can be set to take action. dlswTConnOperState accepts only quiescing and disconnecting, and dlswCircuitState accepts only disconnectPending. The MIB offers no way to re-establish a disconnected circuit, because that is meant to be driven by an end station.
sections.eli5: If you flip many switches one at a time, the machine keeps shouting about it to its friends. Flip them all together and it only shouts once.

sections.title: Worked Management Tasks
sections.content:
The RFC walks through tasks a manager might perform. To connect actively to a TCP partner, create a row in dlswTConnConfigTable with SetupType = activePersistent. To accept any partner, use EntryType = global and SetupType = passive, and block one node with a row marked excluded. When rows overlap, the most specific match wins.

To change an active connection, set the row to notInService, quiesce or disconnect the connection, edit the values, then set the row back to active. To investigate trouble, dlswTConnOperDiscTime and dlswTConnOperDiscReason give the time and cause of a disconnection, and the dlswCircuitDiscReason variables explain why a circuit dropped.

Static directory entries can be preloaded to reduce broadcast searches. The manager gets an index from dlswDirMacCacheNextIndex, creates rows in dlswDirMacTable, and entries with a mask of all 0xFFs take precedence over partial wildcards. To cut trap traffic, set the dlswTrapCntl* objects to disabled or partial.
sections.eli5: The memo gives recipes: how to tell the switch to call a friend, how to stop it taking calls from a stranger, and how to find out why a call dropped.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The section is a single sentence: security issues are not discussed in this memo. The RFC offers no guidance on access control or protection of the configuration objects, even though the MIB lets a manager create and disconnect connections and circuits.
sections.eli5: The memo does not say anything about locking the control panel, so that part is left to whoever builds and runs it.

items.label: connecting
items.desc: DLSw has made a connection request to the transport layer.

items.label: initCapExchange
items.desc: Initial capabilities exchange has been sent.

items.label: connected
items.desc: Partner capabilities known; ready for CanUReach (CUR) messages.

items.label: quiescing
items.desc: Settable; prevents new circuits from being established.

items.label: disconnecting
items.desc: Settable; DLSw is bringing the connection down.

items.label: disconnected
items.desc: The transport layer reports the connection is down.
